A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to find the “missing link” between the two extremes of hadronic physics, namely, the hadrons in the vacuum and those at the chiral restoration phase transition.
the hidden local symmetry is an essential ingredient to understand the physics of heavy-ion collisions and compressed matter.

the vector manifestation in hadronic freedom is a key to the understanding of the mass drop of vector mesons in the chiral restoration phase transition and its consequences in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hadronic freedom in heavy-ion collisions is not an artifact but is a genuine feature of the vector manifestation of the hidden local symmetry.
the vector meson mass drop is not a universal property of QCD but is sensitive to the vacuum change and hence to the nature of the vacuum.
the hadrons, which are the basic degrees of freedom of QCD, do not have the freedom to behave as if the vacuum were free in a medium of finite density or temperature.
